claims.text: The onset and progression of melting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by element-specific diffusion.
Fe atoms have elevated local potential energy relative to the other constituents.
Cu has a lower elemental melting point than the other constituents.
Fe and Cu atoms become mobile at lower temperatures than Ni, Cr, and Co atoms.
Early Fe and Cu mobility initiates the nanoparticle melting transition.
Premelting surface disorder begins in the outer two to three atomic layers.
Locally initiated melting subsequently propagates from the surface into the nanoparticle core.
The transition occurs without formation of a stable, continuous liquid shell.
Elevated Fe local energy or pressure and Cu's lower melting point drive preferential early Fe and Cu mobility.
Preferential Fe and Cu mobility produces high displacement and high local strain in the outer atomic layers.
The melting point follows an inverse-radius dependence.
Larger FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles will have higher melting temperatures than smaller nanoparticles under the specified protocol.
Premelting and melting will not produce significant persistent elemental clustering.
The assumed bulk melting limit is 2184 K.
Conventional surface-liquid-shell models predict premelting through unbound surface atoms forming a persistent liquid shell.
The modeled starting particles are random equiatomic Fe20Ni20Cr20Co20Cu20 FCC nanoparticles with a 3.52 Å lattice parameter.
The proposed comparison varies nanoparticle radius from approximately 5 to 40 Å while retaining the specified composition, potential, and heating protocol.
